# Egami.Barcodes: guide for coding agents

Egami.Barcodes writes and reads barcodes: 1D (Code 128, GS1-128, Code 39, ITF, EAN and UPC and others) and 2D (QR, Data
Matrix, PDF417, Aztec). It draws them onto Egami.Drawing's canvas, so they stay vectors in PDF and SVG output, or onto rasters,
and reads them from rasters.

Namespaces: `Egami.Barcodes`, with `Egami`, `Egami.Pixels` and `Egami.Drawing`.

## Egami's vocabulary

Egami has its own names. Use them, not names from other imaging libraries: Egami has no `Image` type, no `Mutate` or `Clone`
and no `Configuration`.

- `Raster` and `Raster<TPixel>` hold an image; `TPixel` is a pixel type such as `Rgba8`, `Rgb8`, `Gray8`, `Bgra8` or `RgbaF32`
  (namespace `Egami.Pixels`). `Raster.Load` returns the type that fits the file; `Raster.Load<Rgba8>` converts while decoding.
- `Raster.Probe` reads a file's size, format and orientation without decoding it.
- `Apply(ops => ...)` changes a raster in place through a chain of operations; `Derive(ops => ...)` returns a new raster.
  `As<TPixel>()` converts to a new raster and `Copy()` duplicates one.
- `Save(path)` picks the writer from the extension; `Save(stream, format, options)` names it. Loading always detects the format
  from the bytes, never from the extension.
- `EgamiContext` holds the settings, `SafetyLimits`, thread count and registered formats a call uses. It is immutable: change
  it with `with`, and pass it to `Load` or `Probe`, or make it the default once at startup with `EgamiContext.SetDefault`.
- Every `Raster` owns pooled pixel memory: dispose it, best with `using`. `Derive`, `As` and `Load` return new rasters that you
  dispose too.

## Entry points

- `Barcode.Create(format, data)`, or one method per symbology such as `Barcode.Qr`, `Barcode.Code128` and `Barcode.DataMatrix`,
  with its options (`QrOptions` and others); `Gs1.Parse` for GS1 element strings.
- `barcode.ToRaster(pixelsPerModule)`: black on white, quiet zone included.
- `canvas.DrawBarcode(barcode, rect, paint)`, and `barcode.ToPath()`: as vectors.
- `raster.ReadBarcodes(options)` and `raster.ReadBarcode(options)`: find and decode; `BarcodeReaderOptions.Formats` limits what
  is looked for.

## Samples

From a table of formats and data:

```csharp
// Labels from a table that stores each barcode's format with its data.
(BarcodeFormat Format, string Data)[] rows =
[
    (BarcodeFormat.Ean13, "590123412345"),
    (BarcodeFormat.Code128, "SHIP-0042"),
    (BarcodeFormat.Qr, "https://inexin.github.io/Egami/"),
];

foreach ((BarcodeFormat format, string data) in rows)
{
    Barcode barcode = Barcode.Create(format, data);
    using Raster<Gray8> image = barcode.ToRaster(pixelsPerModule: 3);
}
```

QR codes:

```csharp
// Level M, raised to Q or H when that fits in the same size; segments chosen for the fewest bits.
Barcode link = Barcode.Qr("https://inexin.github.io/Egami/");

// A fixed size and level, for a layout that must not change.
Barcode fixedSize = Barcode.Qr("ORDER-1180042", new QrOptions { Version = 3, ErrorCorrection = QrErrorCorrection.H });

// Bytes as they are, and GS1 element strings with FNC1.
Barcode bytes = Barcode.Qr([0x45, 0x67, 0x61, 0x6D, 0x69]);
Barcode gs1 = Barcode.Qr(Gs1.Parse("(01)09501101530003(10)AB12"));

using Raster<Gray8> image = link.ToRaster(pixelsPerModule: 4);
```

On a canvas:

```csharp
using Raster<Rgba8> label = Raster.Create(300, 200, Rgba8.White);
using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = label.CreateCanvas())
{
    // Fitted into the rectangle and centered, quiet zone inside it; on a raster, modules snap to whole pixels.
    canvas.DrawBarcode(qr, new RectF(20, 20, 160, 160), Rgba8.Black);
}
```

Reading:

```csharp
// Every barcode in the image, of any format.
foreach (BarcodeResult result in scan.ReadBarcodes())
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{result.Format}: {result.Text} at {result.Corners[0]}");
}
```

## Common mistakes

- Making a small raster and scaling it up, or scaling a barcode image to a size that is not a whole number of pixels per
  module. Pass `pixelsPerModule` to `ToRaster`, or draw with `DrawBarcode`, where modules snap to whole pixels on rasters.
- Cutting off the quiet zone. `ToRaster` and `DrawBarcode` keep it inside the size you give; don't crop it away.
- Reading for every format when you know which one to expect: set `BarcodeReaderOptions.Formats`, so the reader skips the
  others.
- Putting GS1 data into a plain Code 128 or QR string. Parse it with `Gs1.Parse` so the FNC1 characters are right.
